questions.scenario: During every rolling deployment, a few payment requests fail with connection errors as old instances are stopped.
questions.question: Which configuration addresses this?
options: Disabling health checks
Deploying only at midnight
Graceful shutdown (server.shutdown=graceful with a shutdown timeout) so instances finish in-flight requests after SIGTERM, plus readiness probes
Larger container images
questions.explanation: Graceful shutdown stops new requests while completing current ones, and readiness ensures new instances receive traffic only when ready.

questions.scenario: Release 2.4 renames the column narration to description and deploys with a rolling update. Old instances start failing during the rollout.
questions.question: What approach avoids this?
options: Expand and contract: add the new column, write both, backfill, switch reads, and drop the old column in a later release
Run the migration manually after all instances are updated
Edit the original V1 migration to use the new name
Use a recreate deployment so versions never overlap
questions.explanation: During rolling, blue-green and canary releases, old and new versions run together, so every schema change must stay compatible with both.

questions.scenario: A new version passes CI but its error rate jumps after release. The team wants the fastest safe recovery.
questions.question: What should be possible within minutes?
options: Rebuilding the old version from source and retesting it
Restoring last night's database backup
Redeploying the previous image SHA or switching traffic back to the previous revision, without a database restore
Waiting for a fix to be written
questions.explanation: Immutable images and backward-compatible schemas make application rollback a single operation; restores lose data and take hours.

questions.scenario: A team wants to release a new fee engine to 5% of traffic, watch error rates and latency for an hour, then increase gradually.
questions.question: Which strategy is this?
options: Big-bang release
Recreate deployment
Canary release
Blue-green with an instant full switch
questions.explanation: A canary exposes a small share of real traffic to the new version and increases it only while metrics stay healthy.

questions.scenario: You are making a Spring Boot service ready to run on any container platform.
questions.question: Which properties should it have? (Choose two.)
options: Session state stored in the instance's local memory
Configuration and secrets supplied by the environment rather than baked into the image
Liveness and readiness health endpoints
Uploaded files written to the container's local disk
questions.explanation: Environment configuration and health endpoints let any platform run and manage the service. Local state breaks when instances are replaced or scaled.

questions.scenario: On Google Cloud Run, you want to smoke-test a new revision on its own URL before it receives any customer traffic.
questions.question: How can you do this?
options: Use the latest tag
Deploy normally and test quickly
Create a second Google Cloud account
Deploy with --no-traffic and a tag, test the tagged URL, then shift traffic to it
questions.explanation: Tagged revisions get their own URL without serving production traffic, so they can be verified before traffic migration.

questions.scenario: An ECS service's new tasks keep failing health checks after a deployment, and nobody is watching.
questions.question: Which ECS feature limits the damage automatically?
options: Task definition revisions
The deployment circuit breaker with rollback enabled
CloudWatch log retention
Fargate Spot capacity
questions.explanation: The circuit breaker detects that new tasks cannot become healthy and rolls back to the last working deployment.
